help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the first long car journey in history, and the woman who made it: in August 1888 Bertha Benz took her husband's car without asking him, drove with her two sons from Mannheim to Pforzheim, 106 kilometres, repaired the car on the way with a hat pin and a garter, and bought fuel at a pharmacy, which is why that pharmacy is called the first petrol station in the world. All facts are real and were checked. You read it in the past: the modal verbs in the Präteritum (sie wollte, sie musste, sie konnte, sie durfte nicht), war and hatte, and the Perfekt with haben (hat repariert, hat gekauft, hat geschickt). Read for the story first, then look for one problem and one solution per question.
help.tips[0].title: Modal verbs in the past
help.tips[0].text: In stories the modal verbs use the Präteritum, not the Perfekt: wollen → wollte (wanted), müssen → musste (had to), können → konnte (could), dürfen → durfte (was allowed), sollen → sollte, mögen → mochte. No umlaut! Endings like haben: ich musste, du musstest, er musste, wir mussten, sie mussten. The main verb stays at the end: Sie musste den Wagen reparieren.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Bertha wanted to visit her mother, but she was not allowed to take the car.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The car could not climb hills; the sons had to push.
help.tips[0].check.q: Sie ____ Benzin kaufen, aber es gab keine Tankstelle. (müssen, Präteritum)
help.tips[0].check.why: Präteritum of müssen: musste, without umlaut. müsste is a different form (would have to).
help.tips[1].title: Telling a story: Präteritum and Perfekt together
help.tips[1].text: German stories mix two pasts: war, hatte and the modals in the Präteritum (Es war heiß. Sie hatte zwei Söhne. Sie musste tanken.), everything else in the Perfekt (Sie hat getankt. Sie ist weitergefahren). Time words hold the story together: zuerst, dann, danach, später, am Abend, am Ende.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: At first everything was fine. Then the car had no more fuel, and Bertha had to go to the pharmacy.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: In the evening she arrived in Pforzheim and sent her husband a telegram.
help.tips[1].check.q: Which form is right in a story: 'The car was slow'?
help.tips[1].check.why: sein in the past is war; ist gewesen is possible but stories use war.
help.remember[0]: wollte, musste, konnte, durfte, sollte, mochte: no umlaut, main verb at the end.
help.remember[1]: Stories: war, hatte, modals in Präteritum; the other verbs in Perfekt.
help.exam: Short biographical stories in the past with multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: She took the car without asking, drove 106 kilometres with her two sons and fixed the engine with a hat pin. Read about Bertha Benz, 1888.
help.vocab[6].example: Carl hat nur einen Zettel gefunden.
passageTranslation:
In August 1888 it was early morning in Mannheim. Carl Benz was still asleep. His wife Bertha had an idea: she wanted to drive to her mother in Pforzheim with the new car, 106 kilometres. Carl had built the car, but he did not want to show it to anyone. He was afraid: what will people say?

Bertha did not ask. She woke her sons Eugen (15) and Richard (14), and the three set off. Carl only found a note: We are driving to Grandma.

The journey was not easy. The car could only drive 16 kilometres per hour. On the hills the sons had to push. Then the fuel ran out. There were no petrol stations! Bertha had to go to the pharmacy in Wiesloch and buy Ligroin there, a cleaning agent. That pharmacy is today called 'the first petrol station in the world'.

Then the fuel line was blocked. Bertha cleaned it with her hat pin. A cable was broken, and she repaired it with her garter. The brake stopped working, and a shoemaker had to put leather on the brake. That was the first brake-lining repair in history.

In the evening the three arrived in Pforzheim. Bertha sent Carl a telegram: We are safely here. The newspapers wrote about the journey, and suddenly everyone wanted to see the car. Carl Benz later said: without Bertha there is no car.
